question: Why does a solution of ethanoic acid turn blue litmus red?
solution:
The correct answer is __**It is an acid.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ethanoic acid**, also known as **acetic acid**, is a weak organic acid with the chemical formula **CH₃COOH**.
 
• Acids are substances that release **hydrogen ions (H⁺)** when dissolved in water. Ethanoic acid dissociates partially in water to produce hydrogen ions. The presence of these hydrogen ions is what causes acids to exhibit their characteristic properties.
 
• When a blue litmus paper is dipped into the solution of ethanoic acid, it turns red. This is because litmus paper reacts to the presence of hydrogen ions (**H⁺**), which are abundant in acidic solutions. *Hence, the solution turns blue litmus paper red.*
 
• The ability to turn blue litmus paper red is one of the key characteristics of acids, including both strong acids (such as hydrochloric acid) and weak
